result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both define a compact set of duration and easing tokens, and both map every requested pattern in a lookup table. B's reduced-motion column covers each pattern explicitly, while A's reduced-motion section is partly left as notes and a placeholder keyframe. A wins narrowly: it is tighter and easier to use as documentation, and it is clearer about what stays instant (table data, focus rings, the app shell). It also says plainly that the numbers are defaults to tune and explains how to propose a change. B spreads into loading and error policy, and it opens with a note about the Write tool being unavailable. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers define four duration tokens and three easings, and both map every pattern to them. A's spec table gives each pattern its own reduced-motion fallback, which makes it easy to look up and use. B's reduced-motion code is incomplete: it relies on an undefined `fade-in-or-out` keyframe, and setting the row detail to `1fr` leaves collapsed rows taking up space. B is shorter and has a strong rule that table data should never animate, but A wins overall because developers can use it more reliably, even though it's longer and goes beyond the request with the loading guidance.
